diffs.diff: pin count: part has 4 (C D - +), datasheet reading has 5 (C D - + IO)
diffs.evidence: Adafruit's schematic for the 1.2" 8x8 backpack (product 1049 family) has a single header part 'CN1' of deviceset '1X4' plus two STEMMA QT connectors, and only VDD/GND supply nets (no separate IO/Vi2c rail). The Adafruit LED Backpack guide's 1.2" 8x8 assembly says 'We'll assume you want to use a 4pin header ... Solder the four pins' and 'Just connect the VCC+ pin'. The 'IO - I2C bus voltage' pin in the second reading belongs to a different board, the 1.2" 7-segment backpack ('"+" - 5v ... "IO" - I2C bus voltage').

diffs.diff: maximum supply: part 5.5 V, datasheet reading 5 V
diffs.evidence: Holtek HT16K33 datasheet Rev 1.10, D.C. Characteristics: 'VDD Operating Voltage ... 4.5 (min) 5 (typ) 5.5 (max) V'; Absolute Maximum Ratings: 'Supply Voltage VSS-0.3V to VSS+6.5V'. The backpack's + pin feeds the chip's VDD directly (schematic: header + net is VDD, no regulator), so 5.5 V is the maximum; the second reading's 5 V is the typical/nominal value Adafruit quotes ('3.3v or 5v microcontroller').
